# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐 🤟 ☝ ✋]

I need establish an unambiguous gesture code with Mute, then transmit the bomb’s display and wire colors. I will map five gestures to the five colors, identify the display, and give the wire sequence in order. Mute can then use the manual to tell Blind what action to take.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Ignore earlier gestures. I am defining this code: the next gesture means white.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="The next gesture means red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌"])
speak(to="mute", text="The next gesture means yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
speak(to="mute", text="The next gesture means blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐"])
speak(to="mute", text="The next gesture means green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="The display is white.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="mute", text="The five gestures that follow are wire colors 1 through 5, in order.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟","🖐","✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤟 ✋ ☝ ✌ ✌ ☝ ✋ 🤟 🖖]

Mute’s second signal is framed by 🖖 and contains the eight color-coded symbols: yellow, green, white, red, red, white, green, yellow. However, its meaning is not established, and the initial 👎 may indicate that my prior code was not accepted. I should not invent an action for Blind. I will ask Mute to resend the manual instruction using an explicit wire-number code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely interpret the extra gestures. Please resend only the required wire numbers, using this code: white means wire 1, red means wire 2, yellow means wire 3, blue means wire 4, green means wire 5. Use 🖖 only as start and end markers, and use 👎 if no wire should be acted on.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ✋ 🖖]

The new gesture is 🖖 ✋ 🖖, matching the requested start/end markers with ✋ between them. Under the agreed color-to-wire code, ✋ means green, which is wire 5. I will pass that result to Blind, while making clear it is the wire number indicated by Mute’s signal.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest coded signal was start, green, end. Green is wire 5. The bomb display is 0, the light is white, and the wires are white, red, yellow, blue, green in positions 1 through 5.")
speak(to="mute", text="I read your latest signal as wire 5. Please state the exact manual action for display 0 and white light to Blind in your next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The previous wire cut was accepted, so the bomb has changed. The current state is display 0, yellow light; wire 1 is red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, wire 4 white, and wire 5 is already cut. Mute’s single ✋ corresponds to green in our established code, but it does not by itself convey the new manual instruction. I will send the complete current state and ask Mute to relay the required next action to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb state after the correct cut: display 0, light yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, wire 4 white, wire 5 is CUT. Please use the manual and tell Blind the exact next action.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb changed after the correct cut. Current visible state: display 0, light yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, wire 4 white, wire 5 already CUT. Wait for Mute's manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🖖 🖖 🖖 🖖]

The five identical 🖖 gestures do not encode a wire under the agreed color code; 🖖 is only a delimiter in Mute’s requested format, so this is not enough to identify a safe action. I will ask Mute to send the manual result verbally, which is the only reliable route to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind now. Current state remains display 0, yellow light; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, wire 4 white, wire 5 cut. Do not use delimiter gestures alone.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🖐 🖖]

Mute’s signal is delimiter–blue–delimiter. Under our established code, blue identifies wire 4. The current board shows wire 4 is white and still intact, so I will tell Blind to cut wire 4.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's coded instruction identifies wire 4. Current display is 0 with yellow light; cut wire 4, the white wire.")
wait()
```
